methodInfo.straight.title: Straight sets
methodInfo.straight.lead: Do a set, rest, and again. Same exercise until all sets are done.
methodInfo.straight.step1: Do the reps written on the card.
methodInfo.straight.step3: When the rest ends, the next set. {sets} {sets, plural, one {set} other {sets}} in total.
methodInfo.straight.chip2: I didn’t get all the reps, what now?
methodInfo.superset.title: Superset
methodInfo.superset.lead: Two exercises back to back: a short rest between them, a long rest only after both.
methodInfo.superset.step2: A short {short} rest, then the second exercise.
methodInfo.superset.step3: A {long} rest, then back to the first for the next round.
methodInfo.superset.chip1: Why is the rest between them short?
methodInfo.superset.chip2: Can I do them as straight sets?
methodInfo.pyramidWave.lead: Each step is a harder version with fewer reps, up to the peak. Then back down to the easy version.
methodInfo.pyramidWave.step1: Start with an easy version and more reps.
methodInfo.pyramidWave.step2: Each step a harder version and fewer reps, up to the peak.
methodInfo.pyramidWave.step3: On the way back the version gets easier and the reps go up.
methodInfo.pyramidWave.chip1: What if I couldn’t do the peak?
methodInfo.pyramidWave.chip2: Why go back down after the peak?
methodInfo.pyramidPeak.lead: Only upward: each step is harder with fewer reps, and the last step is the peak set.
methodInfo.pyramidPeak.step1: The first step is easy, as a warm-up.
methodInfo.pyramidPeak.step2: Each step is harder, with fewer reps.
methodInfo.pyramidPeak.step3: The peak set: {peak} on the hardest version, fully focused.
methodInfo.pyramidPeak.chip2: What if I couldn’t do the peak?
methodInfo.tabata.title: Tabata
methodInfo.tabata.lead: One clock runs it all: {work} work, {rest} rest, and on to the next exercise.
methodInfo.tabata.step2: {rest} rest, and the clock moves to the next exercise by itself.
